desc_key_9:
Coarse grind. Pour all the water and stir evenly. Let it steep for 4 minutes, then press the plunger down slowly to the bottom.

Flavor Profile: Very thick body, strong aroma, classic gritty texture.
desc_key_10:
Brew a very strong coffee concentrate. Mix it with steamed or heated milk in a 1:1 ratio.

Flavor Profile: Warm, milky, savory milk notes with a strong coffee character.
desc_key_11:
Medium-fine grind. Stir immediately with a spoon at the beginning. Let it steep for 5 minutes. Press the plunger ONLY until it touches the water to keep the fine grounds trapped below.

Flavor Profile: Very clean for a French Press, smooth body, slowly extracted sweetness.
desc_key_12:
Stir vigorously at the beginning and immediately skim the foam in the first minute for even extraction from the start.

Flavor Profile: Thick body with minimal grit, cleaner taste than traditional methods.
desc_key_13:
Pre-infuse with room temperature water for 1 minute, then pour hot water. This reduces bitterness and enhances the coffee's natural sweetness.

Flavor Profile: Reduces sharp acidity and bitterness, highlighting a smoother sweet profile.
desc_key_14:
Similar to cupping. Brew for 4 minutes, stir gently, skim the foam and crust, wait another 5 minutes before pressing.

Flavor Profile: Nordic roast (light) characteristics, bright acidity, light body, more akin to a cupping bowl.
desc_key_15:
[Method: Standard] Use a paper filter. Low water temperature (80°C). Stir quickly for 10 seconds, then press slowly. Do not press until it hisses.

Flavor Profile: Very sweet, low acidity, thick body, similar to espresso concentrate.
desc_key_16:
[Method: Standard] Medium-fine grind. Boiling water. Standard brew (non-inverted). Stir gently, then press slowly at 60 seconds.

Flavor Profile: Clean cup, bright acidity, tastes similar to a V60 pour-over.
desc_key_17:
[Method: Standard] More coffee-efficient. Standard position. Brew for 2 minutes, swirl slightly, let it rest for 30 seconds, then press slowly.

Flavor Profile: Very efficient, sweet, full body, and even extraction without excessive sourness.
desc_key_18:
[Method: Inverted] (MUST be Inverted). Pour water, stir vigorously with a spoon, then attach the cap. At 1:30, carefully flip the brewer onto a cup and press down.

Flavor Profile: Strong body, bold taste, perfect for mixing with milk or drinking black.
desc_key_19:
[Method: Inverted] Shorter brew time, inverted method. Flip at 1:00 and press for 30 seconds.

Flavor Profile: Brighter acidity, clean cup.
desc_key_20:
[Method: Standard] Brew a very strong coffee concentrate (Use a Prismo or Flow Control attachment), then immediately stir with cold milk and ice cubes in a glass.

Flavor Profile: Smooth, creamy, and refreshing milk punch.
desc_key_21:
[Method: Standard] 2023 World Aeropress Championship winning recipe. Low-temperature extraction with intense stirring, then bypassed with hot water at the end.

Flavor Profile: Complex, sweet, bright fruity acidity but with a very silky texture.
desc_key_22:
[Method: Standard] Long 9-minute steep with a V60 grind size. Produces a sweet and even extraction without bitterness.

Flavor Profile: Very high extraction yield (high EY), maximum sweetness, no under-extracted sourness.
desc_key_23:
[Method: Standard] Use inverted or standard method. Boiling water to extract coffee concentrate. Stir evenly, then press over a glass filled with ice chunks.

Flavor Profile: Refreshing, strong initially but melts slowly (refreshing), sweet.
desc_key_24:
[Method: Standard] Very fine grind with very little water, pressed as hard as possible. Produces a thick concentrate similar to espresso.

Flavor Profile: Strong, punchy, creates faux crema (if pressed hard), great for mocktails or milk drinks.
desc_key_25:
Medium-coarse grind. Dark roast Robusta coffee. Tamp down with the press filter. Pour boiling water. The dripping process takes about 5-6 minutes.

Flavor Profile: Strong bitterness, smokey, very thick (syrupy) and bold body.
desc_key_26:
A lighter variation. Use medium-fine grind and Arabica beans. Tamp lightly, drip for 4 minutes.

Flavor Profile: Brighter acidity, lighter body.
desc_key_27:
Use a 1:15 ratio, similar to a standard pour-over, but brewed with the Vietnam Drip. Tamp very lightly.

Flavor Profile: Clean cup, balanced, similar to a slow drip V60.
desc_key_28:
Modern approach for light roast coffee beans. Extracts sweet and sour flavors cleanly.

Flavor Profile: Cleaner than traditional methods, acidity starts to shine, modern flavor complexity.
desc_key_29:
Use an Aeropress paper filter on top of the coffee bed before tamping for a more even water distribution.

Flavor Profile: Higher extraction yield, more balanced.
desc_key_30:
Classic combination of Sweetened Condensed Milk (SCM) and Palm Sugar Syrup. SCM provides the signature 'creamy' texture of Vietnam Drip, while palm sugar adds a sweet caramel aroma. Pour SCM and palm sugar into the bottom of the glass, brew slowly, stir well, then add ice.

Flavor Profile: Very creamy, sweet palm sugar caramel blends with a strong and thick coffee flavor.
desc_key_31:
Place a paper filter (Aeropress size) at the bottom of the Phin brewer before adding coffee. Produces an incredibly clean brew with no fine grounds. (Optional: place another paper filter on top of the coffee before tamping for super even extraction).

Flavor Profile: Much cleaner with no grit, reduced body but with clearer flavor clarity.
desc_key_32:
Designed for specialty coffee beans (Light Roast), the tamping process is less firm to allow optimal water flow.

Flavor Profile: A longer ratio produces a lighter beverage, similar to a strong pour-over.
desc_key_33:
Rare method: Tamp the coffee with the filter press, pour bloom water, then tamp AGAIN (second tamp) before pouring the rest of the water. Results in a much slower drip rate.

Flavor Profile: Incredible extraction intensity, like espresso, with a very thick body.
desc_key_34:
Temperature 93°C. At minute 4, push the back of a cupping spoon 3 times across the coffee surface (break the crust). Skim the remaining foam. Start slurping at minute 10 when the temperature drops.

Flavor Profile: Pure flavor profile of the coffee beans for defect/quality evaluation purposes.
desc_key_35:
Home-style cupping. Use two spoons to skim the foam at minute 4.

Flavor Profile: Pure coffee bean flavor without paper filter interference, perfect for comparing 2 different beans.
desc_key_36:
Focuses on evaluating the coffee flavor when it is very cold at minute 15. The initial phase is the same, but wait much longer.

Flavor Profile: Assesses the coffee flavor at room temperature (highlighting sweetness or alternatively, defects/sourness).
desc_key_37:
No crust breaking process. The coffee grounds are left to sink slowly to the bottom of the glass on their own. Results in a very clean flavor evaluation.

Flavor Profile: Very clean, slower extraction avoiding excessive astringency.
desc_key_38:
Medium-fine grind. Pour hot water over the coffee; the drips will immediately hit the ice cubes in the server to lock in volatile aromas.

Flavor Profile: Very sharp, refreshing, and aromatic fruity acidity (floral/fruity).
desc_key_39:
Similar to Japanese Iced Coffee, but the ice cube ratio is adjusted and the pours are divided to maximize sweetness.

Flavor Profile: Sweeter and more balanced, not overly acidic, with a slightly thicker body.
desc_key_40:
Adaptation of the 2024 World Brewers Cup 3rd Place recipe. Uses 4 pour phases with decreasing volumes at the end to prevent over-extraction. Produces a balanced and syrupy flavor.

Flavor Profile: Layered flavor, high complexity, elegant aromatic sweetness.
desc_key_41:
High temperature (93°C). Very fast water flow (fast flow). Swirl the dripper quite aggressively at the beginning so all grounds are evenly wetted. Finishes very quickly in 2 minutes.

Flavor Profile: Very transparent fruity acidity, light, similar to coffee-flavored sweet tea.
desc_key_42:
Consistent pours for flat-bed drippers. Highlights acidity and flavor clarity.

Flavor Profile: Incredible sweetness thanks to the flat bed, consistent extraction, balanced.
desc_key_43:
Use 85°C water and quick center pours to avoid burnt and excessively bitter flavors in dark roast beans.

Flavor Profile: Smooth bitterness, caramel sweetness, without excessive burnt/smokey notes.
desc_key_44:
Devil Recipe V60 Switch. OPEN the valve at the beginning. MUST use ROOM TEMPERATURE water (cold/normal) for the first 60ml bloom phase. For the rest, use boiling hot water for the immersion phase.

Flavor Profile: Very bold, thick sweet extraction at the start, finished with immersion for body.
desc_key_45:
[Method: Inverted] 2018 World Aeropress Championship winning recipe. Inverted position, vigorous stirring, resulting in a super fruity extraction.

Flavor Profile: Vibrant, bright acidity, clean finish.
desc_key_46:
[Method: Inverted] 2017 Championship recipe. Strong 1:5 ratio at the beginning, topped up with bypass water at the end. Inverted.

Flavor Profile: Round body, balanced, highly recommended for natural processed coffees.
desc_key_47:
[Method: Standard] Standard Aeropress (not inverted). 80°C water, let it drip slowly then press very slowly.

Flavor Profile: Complex, dominantly sweet, juicy body.
desc_key_48:
[Method: Standard] Uses a Prismo cap or Flow Control. Full immersion without being inverted.

Flavor Profile: Like home espresso, strong, no premature water leakage.
desc_key_49:
[Method: Standard] High concentrate extraction resembling espresso. Use Prismo/Flow Control and an espresso grind size.

Flavor Profile: Bitter, thick, bold, perfect for mixing with brown sugar or milk.
desc_key_50:
[Method: Standard] Wide ratio and coarse grind for a refreshing, tea-like coffee flavor.

Flavor Profile: Very light, transparent, dominant floral/fruity notes like premium tea.
desc_key_51:
[Method: Standard] Specifically for Robusta coffee. Short extraction with 85°C temperature so it's not too bitter.

Flavor Profile: Classic Robusta bitterness balanced by a thick texture and sweet nutty notes.
desc_key_52:
Make a salt cream by frothing sweetened condensed milk, liquid milk/cream, and salt until foamy. Drip the coffee over it. Stir before drinking.

Flavor Profile: An amazing combination of savory saltiness, thick sweetness, and bold coffee bitterness. Umami!
desc_key_53:
Whip free-range egg yolks with sweetened condensed milk and a little honey until it fluffs into a thick foam. Drip hot coffee over or under it.

Flavor Profile: Very creamy, dessert-like (tiramisu), thick sweetness, without any eggy smell.
desc_key_54:
A unique Vietnamese combination. Add yogurt to the bottom of the glass, add condensed milk, brew coffee over it, then add ice cubes.

Flavor Profile: Fresh tangy yogurt combined with creamy sweetness and coffee bitterness. Very refreshing.
desc_key_55:
Vietnam Drip specifically for Arabica beans. Lightly tamped, 92°C temperature for a thick yet fruity body.

Flavor Profile: Signature Arabica fruity acidity, body is not as thick compared to Robusta.
desc_key_56:
Add cocoa powder or chocolate syrup into the condensed milk. Drip the coffee through the chocolate. Stir well.

Flavor Profile: Intense dark chocolate, sweet, thick, like a chocolate coffee candy.
desc_key_57:
A variant of Vietnamese iced milk coffee (Bạc Xỉu) with added coconut milk. The proportion of milk and coconut dominates over the coffee for a sweet, savory, and creamy taste.

Flavor Profile: Savory sweet coconut, very creamy, softer background coffee flavor.
extra_key_3: Prepare 80 ml hot water in the serving glass (for bypass)

extra_key_11: Salt Cream (20ml Milk, 10g Condensed Milk, Pinch of Salt), Ice Cubes (100g)
extra_key_12: Egg Yolk (1 unit), Condensed Milk (20g), Honey (1 tsp)
extra_key_13: Plain Yogurt (50g), Condensed Milk (15g), Ice Cubes (100g)
extra_key_15: 40 ml sweetened condensed milk, 60 ml liquid coconut milk, 100 grams ice cubes. (Mix all in the serving glass)
